page: Microsoft Azure M128m is a high-capacity, memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-intensive enterprise environments. Built on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the server utilizes Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 128 dedicated vCPUs spanning 64 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 38 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 3,892 GB of RAM, equating to approximately 30.41 GB of memory per core. The server includes 15,393 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while operating without discrete GPU accelerators and without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark assessments illustrate substantial multi-threaded performance and high memory throughput alongside distinct single-thread architectural constraints. Uncached large-block read operations register 382.78 GB/sec, placing the instance in the upper tier of memory bandwidth benchmarks. Similarly, parallel compute tests such as multi-core stress-ng (87,477.88), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (336.71 GB/sec), and PassMark CPU metrics (52,881.63) place the platform among the top quartile. It also sustains high-density memory operations, reaching 80.7 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread evaluations reflect the lower base frequency of the Xeon processor, showing bottom-decile scores across single-core Geekbench (900.0), single-core stress-ng (1,038.19), and single-threaded gzip compression (17.16 GB/sec).

From an operational and resource perspective, the M128m delivers high memory density per host, making it viable for consolidating vast datasets within a single system boundary instead of distributing across multiple smaller nodes. Due to its balanced multi-core architecture and large integrated SSD footprint, the server is suitable for running large in-memory transactional databases such as SAP HANA, operational distributed caches, heavy business intelligence analytics, and multi-threaded ETL jobs where total RAM capacity and sustained memory bandwidth supersede raw per-core execution speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure M128m is an ultra-high-memory instance tailored for massive in-memory databases and heavy analytics pipelines. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores at 2.7 GHz, supported by 3,892 GB of RAM and 15,393 GB of integrated local SSD storage. The system features no hardware accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional parallel memory bandwidth, achieving 382.78 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations, alongside strong multi-core processing scores and high-throughput memory caching at 80.7 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing metrics and single-threaded compression show modest performance, reflecting its focus on massive horizontal parallelism over raw clock speed. The M128m offers high resource consolidation efficiency for memory-bound systems, making it well matched for enterprise database engines such as SAP HANA, large-scale caching tiers, and in-memory analytics workloads requiring extreme data capacity in a single system image.
